editorial:
You follow Evan McCauley, a troubled man whose strange skills and visions make him think he is losing his mind. When a secret group called the Infinites finds him, they reveal that his memories come from past lives. That setup gives the movie a big, glossy sci-fi hook, with Mark Wahlberg playing a confused hero who slowly learns who he really is. The world has secret bases, reincarnation rules, and two factions fighting over humanity's future, so the story moves fast and keeps throwing new ideas at you.

The action is loud and frequent, with car chases, sword fights, and big set pieces that look great in 4K. Chiwetel Ejiofor makes a strong villain, and Sophie Cookson gives the story some heart. The downside is that the plot can feel rushed and confusing, especially when it explains its reincarnation rules. Still, if you want a flashy action movie with a wild sci-fi idea, this is a fun rental.
endingExplained: In the final showdown, Evan fully remembers his past life as Heinrich Treadway and learns the Egg was hidden inside his own body. Bathurst gets hold of it and tries to activate it on a plane to wipe out all life and stop reincarnation. Evan fights him, takes back the Egg, and stops the device. Bathurst is killed in the crash, while Evan and Nora survive. Evan accepts his identity as an Infinite and chooses to keep protecting humanity's memories.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves flashy sci-fi action and reincarnation stories.
